stem:
A 47-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis has steatorrhea and postprandial bloating. After a fatty meal, duodenal pH falls briefly then normalizes, but his fecal fat remains elevated. Secretin secretion and bicarbonate-rich duct flow are intact on stimulation testing.

Failure of which of the following hormone–product pairings most directly explains persistent fat malabsorption despite acid neutralization?

options.label: A
options.text: Secretin failing to release bicarbonate-rich juice
options.misconception: The acid-neutralizing arm is being blamed though the vignette states it is intact.
options.explanation: The stem specifies intact secretin-driven bicarbonate; steatorrhea with normal acid neutralization implicates deficient enzyme-rich juice instead.

options.label: B
options.text: CCK failing to trigger enzyme-rich acinar secretion
options.misconception: None; fat malabsorption with intact bicarbonate points to lost CCK-driven enzyme release.
options.explanation: Protein and fat in the duodenum stimulate CCK, which drives enzyme-rich juice from pancreatic acini; chronic pancreatitis destroys acini, so CCK cannot restore lipase/protease delivery despite secretin-normalizing pH.

options.label: C
options.text: Gastrin failing to stimulate parietal-cell acid secretion
options.misconception: Gastric acid drive is being treated as the fat-malabsorption mechanism.
options.explanation: Gastrin regulates gastric acid; steatorrhea after a fatty meal implicates inadequate pancreatic enzymes, the CCK-dependent product.

options.label: D
options.text: Motilin failing to initiate migrating motor complexes
options.misconception: Interdigestive motility is being substituted for nutrient-stimulated enzyme secretion.
options.explanation: Motilin governs fasting motility patterns; postprandial fat digestion depends on CCK-driven enzyme release.

options.label: E
options.text: Glucagon failing to inhibit gastric emptying
options.misconception: An unrelated islet hormone is being assigned to duodenal nutrient handling.
options.explanation: Glucagon regulates glucose; fat malabsorption with intact bicarbonate implicates lost CCK-mediated enzyme secretion from damaged acini.

context: Learning objective: separate secretin (bicarbonate, acid neutralization) from CCK (enzyme-rich juice, fat digestion). Intact secretin with steatorrhea localizes the defect to CCK-dependent enzyme release.
